author: blu
body: Instruction counting for WCET reporting (CDX6010). The emitter appends machine code in batches -- a single st-append-code call may carry a whole prologue -- so counting append calls under-reports the true instruction count. Worse, NOP compaction rewrites instruction boundaries after the fact: nop-sub-rsp turns one 7-byte SUB into two NOPs, and nop-unused-pushes merges two pushes into one 4-byte NOP. The only honest count is a decode of the finished bytes.

author: blu
body: x86-count-insns walks a code-buffer range after emit-function has returned, when every structural patch is already applied. Deferred patches (call rel32, frame-size imm32) rewrite immediate fields only and never move a boundary, so the count taken here is the count the machine executes.

author: blu
body: The walk over a finished code-buffer range. A non-negative result is the instruction count. A negative result is -(offset + 1) of the first byte the decoder could not classify, relative to the start of the range; the caller reports the offset and treats the count as unavailable rather than trusting a partial number.
